title: A letter or hands-on help?
hook: How much does application help add beyond information alone?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare control, information, and assisted-application arms as separate interventions.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare control, information, and assisted-application arms as separate interventions.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: An illustrative enrollment table has 6% control, 11% information and 18% assistance. What is the extra assistance-versus-information difference? Toy inputs A=[6, 11, 18]; B=[6, 11, 11].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[5, 7, 12], [5, 0, 5]]. Labels: Info lift pp, Extra help pp, Total lift pp.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Three arms separate contact, information and hands-on help. Combining both treated groups would hide the incremental assistance comparison. These supplied rates permit arithmetic, while causal and transport claims need their own study support.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Control %=6, Information %=11, Assistance %=11. What is Extra help pp? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Control %=6, Information %=11, Assistance %=11. What is Extra help pp?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.section: 19. Public policy nudges: tax, energy, voting
sourceProvenance.text: SNAP enrollment among eligible seniors was 6% with no contact, 11% with an information letter and 18% with help applying (Finkelstein & Notowidigdo, 2019).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.
